issues.legal_issue: A suit for specific performance is not maintainable when the agreement has been terminated and the plaintiff does not seek a declaration that the termination is invalid.
material_facts: The sellers notified the buyer that the sale agreement would be terminated if he did not complete his obligations by the extended deadline.
The buyer did not complete his obligations by that deadline, and the sellers treated the agreement as terminated.
The buyer sued for specific performance and an injunction but did not seek a declaration that the termination was invalid.
issues.conclusion: The suit for specific performance was not maintainable because the agreement had been terminated and the buyer had not sought a declaration challenging that termination.
issues.legal_principle: A plaintiff seeking specific performance on the basis of an agreement that has been terminated must seek a declaration that the termination is invalid; without that relief, the suit for specific performance is not maintainable.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The plaintiff brought a suit seeking specific performance of an agreement.
predicates.agreement_terminated: The other contracting party terminated the agreement after the plaintiff failed to meet the required deadline.
predicates.no_declaration_challenging_termination: The plaintiff did not ask the court to declare the termination invalid.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff seeks specific performance of an agreement that the other party has terminated but does not challenge that termination by seeking a declaration, the suit is not maintainable.

issues.legal_issue: A buyer who fails to perform within the agreed period and does not establish continuing readiness and willingness to perform is not entitled to specific performance of an immovable-property sale agreement.
material_facts: The agreement fixed a period for completing the sale and provided for a limited extension if required permissions were delayed.
The buyer did not pay the balance consideration or complete the sale within the stipulated and extended period.
The buyer's correspondence showed that he sought further time, and the evidence did not establish that he had the funds or arrangements to pay the balance consideration.
The trial court found that the buyer was not ready and willing to perform, but the first appellate court reversed that finding and granted specific performance.
issues.conclusion: The buyer failed to prove readiness and willingness to perform, and the first appellate court erred in granting specific performance; the denial of that relief was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 16(c) of the Specific Relief Act, a plaintiff seeking specific performance must prove readiness and willingness to perform throughout the relevant period, assessed in light of the plaintiff's conduct and the surrounding circumstances. Under Section 55 of the Contract Act, time is not ordinarily of the essence in a sale of immovable property, but the parties' language, the agreement as a whole, and the circumstances may show an intention to require performance within a specified period. The Court applied Smt. Chand Rani v. Smt. Kamal Rani on time stipulations and N.P. Thirugnnam v. Dr. R. Jagan Mohan Rao and P.R. Deb & Associates v. Sunanda Roy on readiness and willingness.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and immovable_property_sale_agreement and agreed_completion_period and buyer_failed_to_complete_within_applicable_period and buyer_did_not_prove_continuing_readiness

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The plaintiff brought a suit seeking specific performance of an agreement.
predicates.immovable_property_sale_agreement: The agreement concerned the sale of immovable property.
predicates.agreed_completion_period: The parties specified a period for completing the sale, including any agreed extension mechanism.
predicates.buyer_failed_to_complete_within_applicab: The buyer did not complete the required performance within the period fixed by the agreement, including any applicable extension.
predicates.buyer_did_not_prove_continuing_readiness: The buyer's conduct and evidence did not establish readiness and willingness to perform throughout the relevant period.

issues.definition: Specific performance should be denied when a buyer seeking enforcement of an immovable-property sale agreement fails to complete within the applicable agreed period and does not prove continuing readiness and willingness.

issues.legal_issue: A subsequent purchaser's purchase after termination of the earlier sale agreement cannot be treated as defeating the buyer's claim on the ground that the purchaser had notice of that agreement.
material_facts: The sellers treated the earlier sale agreement as terminated before conveying the property to the subsequent purchaser.
The subsequent purchaser paid consideration for the property after that termination.
The first appellate court found that the subsequent purchaser was not a bona fide purchaser because of the earlier agreement.
issues.conclusion: Because the earlier agreement had been terminated before the subsequent sale, the challenge to the subsequent purchaser's bona fide status did not arise, and the contrary finding was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Where the earlier sale agreement has terminated before a subsequent purchaser acquires the property for consideration, the earlier agreement does not subsist as a basis for treating the subsequent purchaser as not bona fide.

predicates.specific_performance_dispute: The dispute concerns a claim for specific performance and a later transfer of the same property.
predicates.earlier_agreement_terminated_before_late: The earlier agreement was terminated before the property was transferred to the subsequent purchaser.
predicates.later_purchaser_paid_consideration: The subsequent purchaser paid consideration for the property.

issues.definition: When the earlier agreement was terminated before a subsequent purchaser paid for the property, that earlier agreement does not defeat the later purchase.

issues.legal_issue: A court should not grant specific performance in the exercise of its discretion without considering the parties' agreed remedies and the buyer's failure to perform.
material_facts: The agreement provided for compensation and reimbursement if the sellers failed to comply, and for forfeiture of the advance if the buyer failed to comply.
The buyer failed to perform his contractual obligations and did not establish readiness and willingness to do so.
The first appellate court granted specific performance without considering the agreed remedies in the agreement.
issues.conclusion: The grant of specific performance was unsustainable; the buyer was not entitled to that relief, and the first appellate decree was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 16(c), 20(1) and 20(2) of the Specific Relief Act govern the buyer's obligation to prove readiness and willingness and the court's discretion to grant specific performance. Section 21(2) is also relevant to compensation. In exercising that discretion, the court must consider the contract's agreed remedies and the parties' conduct.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The plaintiff brought a suit seeking specific performance of an agreement.
predicates.contract_specifies_consequences_for_nonp: The agreement sets out consequences or remedies if either party fails to perform.
predicates.buyer_failed_to_perform: The buyer did not perform the obligations required of him under the agreement.
predicates.court_granted_specific_performance_witho: The court granted specific performance without taking account of the agreement's specified remedies and the buyer's failure to perform.

issues.definition: A court's grant of specific performance is unwarranted when the buyer failed to perform, the agreement specifies consequences for nonperformance, and the court grants relief without considering those consequences.
